title: Decimal Operations
subtitle: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide
bounds: Decimals (PROTOCOL §4b): every operand is 0.01-10 with at most 2 decimal places and at most 2 non-zero digits. + and −: answer 0-20, at most one carry or borrow. × and ÷: the digit work is a times-table fact (each digit factor 2-10; ÷ exact, divisor and quotient digits 2-10); answers at most 3 decimal places. Wrong choices: whatever the misreading gives, 0-999.

tiers.name: Add & Subtract
tiers.description: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract.

tiers.name: Decimal × Whole
tiers.description: Multiply the digits, then keep the decimal's places.

tiers.name: Decimal × Decimal
tiers.description: Multiply the digits, then add up the places of both factors.

tiers.name: Decimal ÷ Whole
tiers.description: Share tenths or hundredths: 2.4 ÷ 3 is 24 tenths ÷ 3.

tiers.name: Divide by a Decimal
tiers.description: Move both points the same number of places, then divide.

ALIGN_RIGHT.student: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits. 0.4 is 0.40.
ALIGN_RIGHT.teacher: Right-justifies the digits instead of aligning the points: 0.4 + 0.35 = 0.39.

DROP_PLACE.student: Every digit counts. Write 0.4 as 0.40 so each place has a partner.
DROP_PLACE.teacher: Drops the digit with no partner in the shorter number: 0.4 + 0.35 = 0.7.

BRING_DOWN.student: An empty place is a 0. Write 0.6 as 0.60, then borrow.
BRING_DOWN.teacher: Brings down the bottom digit under an empty place: 0.6 − 0.25 = 0.45.

DECIMAL_AS_WHOLE.student: 10 tenths make 1 whole. 0.8 + 0.5 is 13 tenths, which is 1.3.
DECIMAL_AS_WHOLE.teacher: Adds the decimal parts as whole numbers and never carries: 0.8 + 0.5 = 0.13.

PLACE_LOST.student: Don't drop the decimal point. Count the places and put it back.
PLACE_LOST.teacher: Gives the whole-number digit result with no decimal point: 0.3 × 4 = 12.

EXTRA_PLACE.student: One place too many. 3 tenths × 4 is 12 tenths, which is 1.2.
EXTRA_PLACE.teacher: Puts one extra decimal place in a decimal-by-whole result: 0.3 × 4 = 0.12.

MISSED_PLACE.student: One place too few. Hundredths in, hundredths out: 0.04 × 6 = 0.24.
MISSED_PLACE.teacher: Puts one decimal place too few in the result: 0.04 × 6 = 2.4.

COUNT_PLACES.student: When you multiply, add the places: 0.6 × 0.2 has 1 + 1 = 2 places.
COUNT_PLACES.teacher: Gives the product as many places as the longer factor, as in addition: 0.6 × 0.2 = 1.2.

TOO_MANY_PLACES.teacher: Puts one decimal place too many in a decimal product: 0.6 × 0.2 = 0.012.

BIG_INTO_SMALL.student: 4 ÷ 5 means 4 shared by 5. Each share is less than 1.
BIG_INTO_SMALL.teacher: Divides the larger number by the smaller when the dividend is smaller: 4 ÷ 5 = 1.25.

SHIFT_ONE_SIDE.student: Move both decimal points the same number of places, not just one.
SHIFT_ONE_SIDE.teacher: Shifts the point in only the divisor or only the dividend: 1.2 ÷ 0.3 = 0.4 or 40.

MULT_FOR_DIV.student: Dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger: 2 ÷ 0.5 = 4.
MULT_FOR_DIV.teacher: Multiplies by the decimal divisor ("division makes smaller"): 2 ÷ 0.5 = 1.
